items.title: Show HN: I built Layfare - find stopovers to save money and explore new cities (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: I kept spending two hours at the gate in an airport in cities that I've never seen - London, Zurich, Madrid. So I built Layfare (https://layfare.com). Give it the trip you're planning, and it shows you every city you could stop in for one or more nights, and what it costs compared to flying straight through. Often there's a minimal cost increase, or even a cost savings. If I'm flying to Dubrovnik from Philadelphia in late February, I can actually save over $200 if I stop for a couple of nights in Zurich. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50454692 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

items.title: Show HN: Black Ops II statically recompiled to native ARM64 macOS (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: I grew up with Black Ops 2 and wanted to see if I could make it work on my 2020 MacBook Pro. So I used Claude Opus 5.5 to create a tool that converts your copy of the game (from Steam) to a native ARM64 Mac app, with almost 60fps in all areas. The whole game is statically recompilated ahead-of-time (AOT) and does not use any emulator whatsoever, be it Wine, Crossover or Rosetta. The best thing is the performance, although some heat issues are still to fix. You get to play the whole Campaign, local Multiplayer (with bots) and local Zombies (all DLCs maps; you need to have them in your Steam library obviously) at about 60fps. Split-screen was not in the PC version, but I've been working on it lately; it's coming soon! LAN mode is on the roadmap for later too :) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50449891 Points: 96 # Comments: 41
